title: What is the significance of the Resurrection?
aliases: significance of the resurrection in the bible
summary: The resurrection vindicates Jesus, defeats death, and guarantees the future resurrection of his people.
historical_context: The resurrection is proclaimed in the earliest Christian witness as the vindication of Jesus and the beginning of new-creation hope.
ancient_near_east_context: The claim stands out in a world where death was treated as final, making bodily resurrection a startling theological and historical announcement.
literary_context: The Gospels narrate the empty tomb and appearances, while Acts and the Epistles interpret the event for the church.
covenantal_significance: The resurrection confirms Jesus as Lord and opens the covenant promise of life, justification, and renewal.
interpretive_notes: Keep the bodily, historical claim in view; the New Testament does not treat resurrection as metaphor only.
The resurrection is both vindication and firstfruits, pointing ahead to the future resurrection of believers.
common_questions: Why is the resurrection so important?
How does the resurrection relate to salvation?
What does the resurrection mean for Christians?
